prompt.context: Our client is a health insurance company. In 2007 (two years ago), we helped them develop their strategic plan, which would govern the direction of the company over the next five years. The client has explained the strategy to the individual business units, and asked the units to submit ideas for new initiatives that would support the strategy. The business units have submitted approximately 80 initiatives all together. It is now 2009 and the economy is in a recession. Due to the increased uncertainty in the market and the difficulty in accessing capital, our client will have to be more selective with the initiatives that it selects to move forward.
prompt.question: The client has hired our firm to help them develop the criteria and methodology to enable them to prioritize the initiatives so that they can move forward with implementation as soon as possible. How would you approach developing a prioritization methodology for these 80 initiatives?

clarifying_info.q: What are the strategic goals outlined in the strategic plan?
clarifying_info.a: The strategic plan included 3 main goals: (1) Increasing scale of the business — increasing sales volume and improving administrative efficiency; (2) Increasing customer involvement in insurance plan selection — creating programs/tools for customers to take ownership of plan selection, an industry trend the client does not want to miss; (3) Rebuilding the brand — positioning as a 21st century healthcare insurance provider and attracting new customers. All three goals are equally important.

clarifying_info.q: Can an initiative support more than one goal?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, an initiative can support more than one goal.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client want equal coverage across goals?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the client wants diversification within all chosen initiatives so there will be an equal distribution of initiatives supporting the three goals.

clarifying_info.q: How quickly does the client want to see results?
clarifying_info.a: Due to the difficult economic situation, it is important to the client to see results and impact of initiatives as quickly as possible.

clarifying_info.q: Who will evaluate the fit of each initiative with the strategic goals?
clarifying_info.a: There is a steering committee that understands the work of the individual business units and will impartially evaluate the effectiveness of each initiative in addressing the strategic goals.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have a preference for quantitative vs. qualitative measures?
clarifying_info.a: The company prides itself on being very data driven and is looking for as quantitative a measure as possible.

exhibits.title: Sample Initiative Rankings by Strategic Goal
exhibits.shows: A ranking table with 4 sample initiatives (A, B, C, D) scored against two strategic goals. Rankings run from 1 (poorest fit) to 4 (best fit) for each goal; N/A indicates the initiative does not address that goal.

framework: Clarify strategic goals and client constraints (3 goals equally weighted, equal distribution required, speed of results critical, data-driven preference)

Develop strategic fit scoring: have steering committee rank each initiative's fit with each goal on a comparable scale; normalize ranks so they are comparable across goals; compute weighted average overall score
Apply financial attractiveness analysis: in recessionary environment prioritize payback period as leading indicator; supplement with NPV (magnitude) and IRR (efficiency/effectiveness)
Stratify initiatives into tiers: Tier 1 = addresses all 3 goals, Tier 2 = addresses 2 goals, Tier 3 = addresses 1 goal; within each tier rank by combined strategic score and financial metrics
Consider qualitative overlay: synergies between initiatives, political considerations across business units, breadth/diversification, competitor responses
Present final ranked list to steering committee with clear methodology documentation

questions.prompt: The steering committee has ranked 4 initiatives across 2 goals using Chart A (rank 4 = best fit, rank 1 = poorest fit, N/A = does not address goal). How would you derive a single overall score for each initiative?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose taking a weighted average of the goal ranks. Because all goals are equally important, weights should be 50%-50% for two goals. Initiatives with N/A for a goal should receive a rank of 0 for that goal. Candidate must also recognize that when goals have different numbers of initiatives, the raw ranks are not directly comparable and must be equalized/normalized before averaging. In this example, Goal 2 only has 2 initiatives ranked 1 and 2, while Goal 1 has 4 ranked 1-4; the Goal 2 ranks need to be adjusted to the same scale as Goal 1 (rank 1 → 3, rank 2 → 4, so that the best in Goal 2 equals the best in Goal 1).

math.setup: Normalize Goal 2 ranks to match Goal 1's 1-4 scale: Goal 2 rank 2 (best) → 4, Goal 2 rank 1 (second best) → 3. N/A = 0. Overall score = 0.5 × (Goal 1 rank) + 0.5 × (Adjusted Goal 2 rank).
math.answer: A=0.5, B=1.0, C=3.5, D=3.5. Initiatives C and D tie at 3.5, requiring further analysis.

questions.prompt: Initiatives C and D tie at 3.5 under the ranking system. What would you do next to break the tie?
questions.guidance: Candidate should suggest assessing the financial attractiveness of each initiative. In the context of the 2009 recession and difficulty accessing capital, the primary financial indicator should be payback period (how quickly the investment pays for itself). This can be supplemented by NPV (to understand the magnitude of value created) and IRR (to understand efficiency/return on investment). The candidate should explicitly justify the emphasis on payback period given the economic environment and need for quick results.

questions.prompt: Now that you understand the client's ranking methodology, how would you structure the full prioritization plan for all 80 initiatives?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose a tiered structure driven by strategic fit, then financials. Example: Tier 1 = initiatives addressing all 3 goals; Tier 2 = initiatives addressing 2 goals; Tier 3 = initiatives addressing 1 goal. Within each tier, rank by weighted average strategic score and then by payback period (or combined financial score). Candidate should demonstrate logical simplicity — avoid over-engineering the model. The methodology should be intuitive and defensible to a steering committee.

brainstorming.prompt: What qualitative considerations should be taken into account alongside the quantitative scoring when selecting initiatives?

categories.name: Synergies
ideas: Initiatives that share resources or infrastructure may reduce combined costs
Initiatives that reinforce each other may increase total value delivered

categories.name: Political & Organizational
ideas: Business units may have political stakes in certain initiatives
Fairness of selection across units may affect organizational buy-in
Steering committee impartiality needs to be maintained

categories.name: Diversification & Breadth
ideas: Ensure equal distribution of selected initiatives across all three strategic goals
Avoid over-concentration in one business unit or one type of initiative

categories.name: External Environment
ideas: Competitor responses to the client's new initiatives
Regulatory changes in health insurance that may affect feasibility
Economic recovery timeline affecting capital availability

categories.name: Implementation Risk
ideas: Ease of implementation and readiness of the business unit
Dependencies between initiatives that affect sequencing

recommendation: Propose a two-stage prioritization methodology: (1) Strategic fit scoring — steering committee ranks each initiative against each of the three goals on a 1-to-80 scale; equalize ranks across goals; compute 33%/33%/33% weighted average overall strategic score; stratify into tiers by number of goals addressed. (2) Financial overlay — within each tier, rank by payback period as primary criterion, supplemented by NPV and IRR.

Recommend the client move forward with initiatives in Tier 1 first (all three goals addressed), selecting an equal number supporting each goal, subject to capital constraints. Apply payback period cutoff appropriate to the current recessionary environment.
risks: Ranking quality depends on the steering committee's consistency and impartiality across 80 initiatives
Payback period estimates may be uncertain in a recessionary environment
Equal distribution across goals may force selection of lower-quality initiatives in a goal area with fewer strong candidates
Synergies between initiatives are not captured in individual scoring
next_steps: Have steering committee complete full ranking of all 80 initiatives
Collect financial projections (cost, revenue, timing) from business units to compute payback period and NPV
Validate tiering thresholds and financial cutoffs with client leadership
Develop a governance process for re-evaluating the initiative list as economic conditions change
